reply:
You're absolutely right, thanks for the correction. I misspoke—`git stash` only stashes *tracked* changes by default. Since your new file was untracked, it wasn't stashed and remained in the working tree.

To include untracked files, you need `git stash -u` (or `--include-untracked`). And to also grab ignored files, use `git stash -a` (or `--all`).

So in your case, running `git stash -u` would have properly stashed that new file before you switched branches.
